memory_lessons.applicability: Test whether compact staging's measured benefit at 128 threads also applies to the current 192-thread configuration.
memory_lessons.claim: The 128-thread compact-source experiment was correct and measured 0.00089008 s, compared with 0.00096318 s for the measured 128-thread full-record configuration. These results do not establish the cause of the difference or predict the 192-thread result.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure compact source staging with the 192-thread CTA under the official protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: At the current 192-thread CTA/tile setting, replacing 28-byte staged Particle records with 16-byte source records reduces dynamic shared memory from 5,376 to 3,072 bytes while retaining the same one-target-per-thread mapping, source order, and barriers. Compact staging was measured as valid and faster at 128 threads, but it is not known whether the benefit carries over to 192 threads or offsets the staging costs; the official measurements should test that assumption.

retained: Keep block and items_per_block at 192, with exactly one target per thread and source tiles of 192 particles.
Stage only source x, y, z, and mass in a 16-byte shared-memory record, reducing the allocation to 3,072 bytes while preserving ascending source interaction order and force arithmetic.
Retain both CTA-wide barriers, partial source-tile handling, and target/output bounds checks.
